The forest was dark. Almost to dark. Weaving in and out through the trees were three separate streaks of black smoke. As they flew the black streaks hungrily absorbed every shadow they passed over, and in turn their smoke trails grew thick and long. For several miles they flew, deep into the bowels of the Forest of Brotherhood. With an abrupt halt, the smoke stopped still. Slowly the three plumes of smoke began to form a crude dome of smoke and shadows. Nearby shadows flickers and flew towards the dome as it grew heavy with the darkness.

As if on cue, the moon began to cast its light through the trees, and the dome took notice and began to clear. Kneeling in the grass where the dome once stood were three female creatures. They were known as Night Wraiths, and their father- the God Cruxius had only just created them a fortnight ago. Lilith the bald girl with a pale complexion and vibrant red scars, Azazel-The green-skinned girl with a mane of long black-red hair, and Pandora-the black haired beauty with piercing eyes and chiseled cheek bones. We all go though things, like you said. Your story doesn't sound too different from mine. I was living in another city, far away from family and relatives attending a college and living in an old house I split with two roommates. My car was back home, in a state of disrepair and I rode my bike everyday to school. I worked at the local hospital, around the corner from where I lived, within walking distance. One night after work, while walking home, I saw a bunch of flashing yellow service lights. Thinking nothing of it, I continued walking as it began to snow for the first time that year. As I got closer, I saw a news van and a crowd gathered around my home where a woman had driven off the road and into my house (it sat on the side of a hill below the road). She had managed to rip the breaker from the wall, thus disconnecting the power completely. With nowhere else to go, I nearly froze to death.

Two days later I'm in the infirmary at the University where they told me I caught pneumonia and almost died. A day later my girlfriend left me for my best friend (at the time). Luckily, a friend of mine picked me up and brought me back home, where I was able to pick up my newly repaired car. A deer ran into me while I was driving not two days later. I od'd on a handful of pills and alcohol, had to be rushed to the hospital. Almost died again. I drove away from my grandmothers house a couple of days later in my car (that somehow managed the deer smashing into it, albeit battle weary), to find out a week later that that was the last time I would see her alive.

The amount of substances I consumed within this two week period should have killed a normal human being. I can't remember being sober for a month after that.

One day, I looked back at old pictures of myself when I had been more 'successful' and realized that it had been my own decision to pursue the path of destruction I had been on for so long. I still had friends and family around me who cared about me, and that was enough for me to keep going on. I am actually thankful for going through that time now. I survived and came out stronger on the other side. We aren't alone and your story has shown me that there is at least one person out there who has lived through something as terrible as I have.

Stay strong, everyone. Sometimes things just have to get worse before they can get better.
